items.question: What do we call an animal that eats both plants and animals?
items.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Bears, crows and humans are omnivores. Herbivores eat only plants and carnivores eat only animals.

items.question: Green plants are called producers in a food chain.
items.explanation: Green plants produce (make) their own food using sunlight. All animals depend on them, directly or indirectly. So every food chain starts with a producer.

items.question: In the food chain grass → deer → tiger, which one is the carnivore?
items.explanation: A carnivore is an animal that eats other animals. The tiger eats the deer, so it is the carnivore. The deer eats grass, so it is a herbivore, and grass is the producer.

items.question: Bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals are called ___.
items.explanation: Decomposers break dead things into simple substances that go back into the soil. Plants then use these as nutrients. Without decomposers, dead leaves and animals would pile up everywhere.

items.question: Bees help plants make seeds by carrying ___ from flower to flower.
items.explanation: Pollen is a fine powder made in flowers. When bees visit flowers for nectar, pollen sticks to their bodies and is carried to the next flower. This is called pollination, and it helps the plant form seeds.
